notes.claim: A power's index shows how many times a number has been multiplied by itself.
With the same base, multiplying powers adds the indices: 9³ × 9⁵ = 9⁸.
Dividing powers of one base cancels common factors: three eights from the top and all those below leave 8 × 8, which is 8².
Raising a power to a power multiplies the indices.

sources.quote: The base numbers are the same (9), so add the indices together (3 + 5 = 8). 9³ x 9⁵ = 9⁸

sources.quote: Three of the eights from the top row and all of the eights on the bottom row have been crossed out – leaving eight multiplied by eight equals eight squared.
